frozen_candidate_root_contribution: An impassable tightness / constriction — a straitening that closes off room to move, breathe, or act. In its most literal packet witness (6:125, صدره ضيقا حرجا) it names an extreme narrowing of the chest; generalized, it is the binding, hemming-in that leaves no give.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: An impassable tightness / constriction — a straitening that closes off room to move, breathe, or act. In its most literal packet witness (6:125, صدره ضيقا حرجا) it names an extreme narrowing of the chest; generalized, it is the binding, hemming-in that leaves no give.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation: The root ح ر ج carries the sense of being hemmed in with no room — a constricting tightness. You see it plainly where the Quran describes a chest made "narrow and حرجا" (6:125) or a constriction "in your chest" (7:2), and an inner tightness/resistance one might "find in oneself" about a judgment (4:65). The large family of legal verses all use the fixed formula "there is no حرج upon so-and-so" — over the blind, lame, sick, the weak, the Prophet, the believers (24:61, 48:17, 9:91, 33:37-50, 22:78, 5:6). There the same core sense operates: no constricting restriction/burden is laid upon them. The formula's "no ... upon" contributes the removal/exemption; the domain (religion, ablution, adoption law) is context; what is left in every case is the notion of a straitening tightness. Even the abstract legal uses read cleanly as "no binding constraint is placed on you," not as a separate meaning.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: FORM: 14× the noun/masdar حَرَج, 1× the adjective حَرِج (6:125). CONSTRUCTION: 13 of 15 sit in the negated-exemption frame "لا/ليس/ما ... [مِنْ] حَرَجٍ ... عَلَى X" — the frame supplies "there is no X upon/for someone" (removal), and مِنْ adds partitive "any." CONTEXT supplies the domain: cultic law (5:6 ablution/tayammum), war exemption (9:91, 48:17), commensality (24:61), marriage/adoption law (33:37,38,50), religion broadly (22:78), acceptance of judgment (4:65), reception of revelation (7:2), divine sealing of a heart (6:125). Subtract all three layers and the invariant residue is a constricting tightness/straitening. The residue is non-empty and does the real work in the two non-formulaic chest verses (6:125, 7:2) and the inner-resistance verse (4:65), where no legal-exemption frame is present.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The purely legal-permission verses 33:37, 33:38, 33:50 are the hardest: there "no حرج upon the Prophet/the believers" concerning marrying adopted sons' ex-wives reads most naturally in English as "no blame/sin," which could suggest the root means culpability rather than constriction. However, the constriction reading still fits — the removal of a binding legal restriction that would otherwise hem the person in — and, decisively, 24:61 places حرج and جناح side by side in one verse, showing the Quran does not treat حرج as the blame-word (that is جناح); حرج is the straitening these persons are freed from.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The strongest rival is root = "blame / sin / culpability," fitting the many "there is no حرج upon" exemption verses. It is rejected because (a) it cannot cover 6:125 (a chest made "narrow, حرجا") or 7:2 (constriction "in your chest") or 4:65 (a tightness "found within themselves"), which have no legal-blame content; (b) 24:61 contrasts حرج with جناح in a single verse, assigning the blame role to جناح, not حرج. The constriction hypothesis subsumes all 15 occurrences; the blame hypothesis is itself a context-derived gloss of the exemption frame.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Against ض ي ق (narrowness): 6:125 pairs ضيقا with حرجا, treating حرج as an intensification — an impassable, extreme constriction beyond ordinary narrowness — so the two are related but not identical, حرج being the tighter, more closed-off pole. Against ج ن ح (جناح, culpable tilt/blame): 24:61 uses both in one verse, isolating حرج as the constriction/hardship term and جناح as the blame term. Against ع ن ت (hardship/distress): حرج is specifically spatial-constrictive (no room), not generic hardship. The residue is thus distinctive and falsifiable: it would fail if some occurrence required "openness/ease" or pure "sin" with no straitening sense — none does.
internal_discovery.rationale: All 15 confirmed occurrences reduce to one invariant residue — impassable constricting tightness/straitening — after subtracting the negated-exemption construction, the masdar/adjective form, and domain context. The reading is anchored, not inferred, by the two non-formulaic chest verses (6:125 adjective beside ضيق; 7:2) and the inner-resistance verse (4:65), which exhibit the literal constriction with no legal frame. The 13 exemption verses then follow as the same residue applied to obligation ("no straitening restriction upon X"). Two independent intra-packet contrasts secure distinctiveness: حرج intensifies ضيق (6:125) and is differentiated from جناح/blame (24:61). No occurrence resists; universal presence holds. Strength is STRONG rather than absolute only because the majority legal uses are frame-driven and, taken alone, could be misread as "blame" — but the packet's own juxtapositions settle this against the rival.

adversarial_verification.notes: Adversarial refutation failed to find any unreconciled occurrence across all 15 (full coverage accounted for). Two clusters. Cluster A (affirmed, inner): 6:125 (ADJ, صدره ضيقا حرجا — literal impassable chest-narrowing), 7:2 (حرج في صدرك), 4:65 (حرجا في أنفسهم — inner constriction/resistance) demonstrate the contribution directly from the packet text. Cluster B (legal, mostly negated لا/ليس...حرج): 22:78, 5:6, 33:37, 33:38, 33:50, 24:61x3, 48:17x3, 9:91 — here حرج is standardly glossed 'blame/sin,' the adversarial pressure point. But each is coherent as the lifted binding constraint (no hemming into an impossible/tight obligation → room to act: eat, marry, be excused from war). 5:6 confirms this internally by contrasting حرج with God not wanting to burden (يريد ليطهركم), framing حرج as imposed constriction/hardship, not mere juridical guilt. No occurrence affirms حرج in a sense incompatible with constriction (none = reward/permission/expansion), so the negated legal uses instantiate the residue as the thing negated. Distinctiveness vs nearest root Dyq (ضيق) is strong: co-occurrence in 6:125 (ضيقا حرجا) shows حرج is not redundant with ضيق but its intensive, impassable degree ('no give / cannot pass') — exactly the proposed residue. Falsifiable and not falsified: claim predicts closing-off/no-room in every occurrence; a positive/expansive حرج would refute it and none exists. Caveat: Cluster B's residue is carried metaphorically (constraint/being hemmed-in) rather than physical narrowing, but it is coherent everywhere and text-internally anchored by Cluster A and by 5:6, so universal presence holds under non-negotiable root unity.
